newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures ended the year on a sour note as stronger-than-expected U.S. economic data upset bond markets in thin trading conditions ahead of the New Year holiday.

The March bond future tumbled from 129.14 before the release of November U.S. new home sales figures and a consumer confidence index to settle at 128.30, its lowest level since December 19. Volume was a paltry 16,619 contracts.
PIBOR contracts, which settled before the release of the U.S. data ended on a positive note, with the March contract within a whisker of its contract high.
The French finance ministry's announcement of its bond sale programme for 1997 was mildly positive as the overall figure was at the lower end of expectations, analysts said.
The ministry said it planned to sell 600 billion francs of OATs and BTANs in 1997, up from total 1996 sales of 562 billion.

"I think it's good," Iain Lindsay, senior bond analyst at Credit Lyonnais said. "I don't think it's going to cause too much alarm as it looks like they're trying to keep the supply down to the lower end of the range."
Most analysts said they expected a figure of 620 billion francs although the forecasts ranged from 600 to 630 billion.
The provisional total for OAT sales was in line with most predictions at 320 billion but projected BTAN sales were 20 billion francs lower than most forecasts at 280 billion.

The first OAT auction for 1997 was scheduled to take place on Thursday. The Treasury will put the new 10-year bond, the 5.5 percent April 2007 OAT, on sale for the first time along with the TEC 10 variable rate OAT.
